1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing on every screen.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case with no italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs.

3.why: Screens are single-column, narrow, and clearly laid out for a mobile viewport.

4.why: All instructions are brief sentences in plain everyday language.

5.why: Recovery-code field shows a format placeholder (ABCD-EFGH-JKLM), but confirmation and TOTP code fields give no example of expected input.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long block of text; copy is short everywhere.

7.why: Setup key, otpauth URI and recovery codes are shown as text but no copy buttons or obvious one-tap copy controls appear.

8.why: Authenticator enrolment shows only a manual setup key and provisioning URI; no QR code is present despite text mentioning scanning.

9.why: Standard email/password inputs on login are compatible with browser autofill and password managers; OTP fields are ordinary text inputs.

10.why: Large page headings and a single prominent blue primary button make the current step and main action obvious.

11.why: Most screens ask for one primary action; authenticator setup pairs key display with code entry, which is the only combined step.

12.why: Success states such as “Authenticator enabled” and “Recovery code accepted and permanently used” clearly say what happened and what to do next.

13.why: Users can regenerate recovery codes, cancel/sign out, and retry steps with no visible penalty; resend for the SMS code is not shown.

14.why: The only error shown is the generic “We could not complete that request. Please try again,” which neither names the problem nor how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown timers or reading/entry time limits appear on any screen.
